text:
Anya: Heads-up — noticed a correlated ECC / Xid spike in us-west-2 last night across 3 machines (gpu-node-47, gpu-node-52, gpu-node-53). They all briefly drained and we saw a flurry of short-lived evictions. Digging into patterns; posting notes so we can decide changes to dashboards/alerts and reduce replacement churn.

Sam: Can you paste the query you used and the rough timeline? Also which autoscaler decided to replace nodes?

Anya: Timeline: 02:14–02:37 UTC. Spike starts ~02:16, first drain 02:20, two more drains 02:28/02:33. Autoscaler = node-proxy-autoscaler v1.4 (policy: immediate eject on 3 XID errors within 5m). Query I used: `sum by(node) (increase(nvidia_gpu_ecc_uncorrectable_total[10m]))` + `sum by(node) (increase(nvidia_gpu_xid_errors_total[10m]))`.

Kevin: Thx. Do we have temp or power glitches correlated? Maybe a local PSU flapping. Also want to see corrected ECC counts: `increase(nvidia_gpu_ecc_correctable_total[1h])`.

Anya: Good call — temps were normal. PSU telemetry showed one node with a 20s power sag at 02:15 on node-52 (cloud vendor metric). But node-47 and node-53 didn't. So maybe intermittent card flakiness combined with strict autoscaler rules.

Liz: This matches other small incidents where cards emit one-off XID bursts then recover. We're hurting ourselves by replacing entire machines on short blips. Can we adjust health scoring to require sustained signals?

Anya: Proposal: new per-GPU health score = weighted sum of signals over 1h with decay. Components: ECC_uncorrectable_rate (weight 0.5), XID_rate (0.3), corrected_ecc_rate (0.1), consecutive_restarts (0.1). Use exponential decay window alpha=0.25 to emphasize recent events but avoid instant ejection. If health_score > 0.7 for 30m -> mark for evacuation. If 0.4–0.7 -> escalate to oncall but wait 2h before auto-eject.

Sam: That sounds reasonable. Can you sketch the PromQL-ish health_score?

Anya: Rough PromQL pseudo: 
```
ecc = clamp_min(sum by(node) (increase(nvidia_gpu_ecc_uncorrectable_total[1h])) / instance_gpu_hours, 0)
xid = clamp_min(sum by(node) (increase(nvidia_gpu_xid_errors_total[1h])) / instance_gpu_hours, 0)
corrected = sum by(node) (increase(nvidia_gpu_ecc_correctable_total[1h])) / instance_gpu_hours
health = 0.5 * normalize(ecc) + 0.3 * normalize(xid) + 0.1 * normalize(corrected) + 0.1 * normalize(consecutive_restarts)
```
normalize() maps metric to 0..1 using a tunable 95th percentile baseline per-region.

Kevin: For dashboards, we should show both raw rates and the composite score so ops can see false positives. Panel ideas: per-region heatmap of health_score, time-series of raw ECC/Xid, event overlay of node drains/evictions, and a small table of current nodes above 0.4. Also add a histogram of inter-event gaps to detect flappy cards.

Liz: SLO conversation: we currently measure region-level GPU availability at 99.95% monthly (counts nodes available vs total capacity). Short-lived recoveries that auto-eject and replace cause extra downtime. If we reduce replacements, we might improve availability but risk leaving a degraded card in place. What's our risk tolerance?

Sam: Ops tradeoff: avoid cascading churn vs. risk of slow degradation. Proposal: two-tier SLOs: (1) availability (hard) 99.95% monthly; (2) incident churn (soft) target max 3 auto-replacements per 1000 GPU-hours. If churn > target, trigger review.

Anya: Implementation plan:
- Create Grafana dashboard `infra/gpu/eviction-correlation` with panels Kevin listed.
- Add health_score as recording rule in Prometheus (name: infra_gpu_health_score).
- Modify autoscaler to consult infra_gpu_health_score and require sustained >0.7 for 30m before auto-eject. Fallback: still allow manual eject.
- Add an alert `GPUCardFlapPossible` when small bursts of XID/ECC occur: amplitude XID>5 in 5m but health_score<0.4 -> warn oncall but do not auto-eject.

Kevin: I'll take the dashboard. I'll add a panel that overlays node-proxy-autoscaler actions: `kube_node_ejections_total` and annotate evictions.

Liz: I'll draft updated SLO wording and a short risk matrix (leave vs eject). Also propose a cooldown policy: once we suppress an auto-eject, escalate if the node shows repeated spikes within 24h.

Sam: For rollout: canary change to autoscaler in us-west-2 pool only for 48h, monitor health_score false negative/positive rates. Metrics to watch: number of ejections, average recovery time, any increase in corrected ECC accumulation.

Anya: Notes on cost: replacing nodes frequently increases cloud spend (replacement + reimage + reattach storage). Rough estimate: each replacement ~ $250 in one-off ops + lost capacity; reducing 5 replacements/month in a region saves ~ $1250 + reduces SLO noise.

Kevin: One more thing — add node labeling so we can quarantine suspicious nodes without full replacement: `gpu.quarantine=true` which moves workloads to spillover pools but keeps node for post-mortem. Less disruptive and quicker rollback.

oncall-bot: [02:40] Incident created: INC-2028-2207 (gpu-eviction-spike-us-west-2). Assigned to oncall team.

Anya: Action items and owners:
- Kevin -> dashboard `infra/gpu/eviction-correlation` (ETA 24h).
- Anya -> draft Prometheus recording rule + tests (ETA 48h).
- Liz -> SLO wording and risk matrix (ETA 72h).
- Sam -> prepare autoscaler canary config + rollback plan (ETA 48h).

Liz: +1. Let's meet tomorrow 14:00 UTC for a quick sync after Kevin posts dashboard.

Sam: Ping me when dashboard ready, I'll pair with Kevin to define alert thresholds.

Anya: Thanks all. Posting the node list and raw logs to the incident channel now for anyone who wants to look.

Kevin: Uploaded small panel mock and the overlay queries to #eng-infra. Will iterate. :thumbsup:
